oneLiner: A collection of guides for rebuilding well-known technologies from scratch, such as a database, a Git client or a shell.
useWhen: You learn best by rebuilding a tool piece by piece and already know one programming language.
skipWhen: You need a production-ready library. These are teaching projects, and guide quality varies by author.

oneLiner: Visual step-by-step roadmaps for roles and skills such as frontend, backend and DevOps.
useWhen: You don't know what to learn next on your career path.
skipWhen: You want hands-on practice. Roadmaps list topics but don't teach them.

oneLiner: A large, community-maintained index of free books, courses and interactive tutorials in many languages.
useWhen: You want free learning material for a specific language or topic.
skipWhen: You want one recommended path. It is an index, so you must pick and judge quality yourself.

oneLiner: Lists of tutorials that teach programming by building a complete project, organised by language.
useWhen: You know the basics of a language and want a project to build next.
skipWhen: You need theory or reference documentation. Tutorials vary in age, so check the dates first.

oneLiner: A study guide to designing large-scale systems, with diagrams, trade-off notes and practice questions.
useWhen: You are preparing for system design interviews or learning how scalable systems fit together.
skipWhen: You need vendor-specific or very recent guidance. It teaches fundamentals, so check newer sources for details.

oneLiner: A long, structured self-study plan for software engineering interviews, from data structures to system design.
useWhen: You want a complete study plan and have months to follow it.
skipWhen: You have only a few weeks or already work with these topics. It is very long and not tailored to specific companies.

oneLiner: Readable Python implementations of many algorithms and data structures.
useWhen: You want to read how an algorithm works in plain Python, or study alongside a visualizer.
skipWhen: You need fast, production-grade code. Use the standard library or tested packages such as NumPy instead.

oneLiner: A very fast command-line search tool that respects .gitignore by default.
useWhen: You search large codebases from the terminal and want speed and sensible defaults.
skipWhen: You need lookaround regex features. Those require ripgrep's optional PCRE2 mode.

oneLiner: A general-purpose fuzzy finder for the terminal that filters any list as you type.
useWhen: You want to find files, shell history entries or Git branches quickly from your shell.
skipWhen: You navigate only with a graphical editor. Most of its value comes from shell integration.

oneLiner: A terminal interface for Git that turns common commands into keyboard-driven screens.
useWhen: You use Git daily and want to stage, rebase and resolve conflicts without typing every command.
skipWhen: You are still learning how Git works. Learn the commands first so you know what the interface is doing.

oneLiner: Community-written cheat sheets showing the most common examples for command-line tools.
useWhen: You know a command exists but forget its flags.
skipWhen: You need complete option references. Use the tool's own man page for that.

oneLiner: A cat clone with syntax highlighting, line numbers and Git integration.
useWhen: You read files in the terminal and want readable output.
skipWhen: You pipe output into scripts and need it raw. Use plain cat, or bat's plain mode.

oneLiner: A browser-based whiteboard for sketching diagrams with a hand-drawn look.
useWhen: You want a quick diagram for docs, slides or a design discussion.
skipWhen: You need strict, formal diagrams such as UML with precise alignment. A dedicated diagramming tool fits better.

oneLiner: A categorized list of free public APIs for developers.
useWhen: You need a data source for a side project or prototype.
skipWhen: You need guaranteed uptime or terms you can rely on in production. Check each API's auth, limits and status first.

oneLiner: A collection of wordlists for security testing: usernames, passwords, URL paths and fuzzing patterns.
useWhen: You run authorized security tests and need wordlists for discovery or fuzzing. Use only on systems you own or have written permission to test.
skipWhen: You lack permission to test the target, or need a small focused list. The full collection is large.

oneLiner: A reference of payloads and bypass techniques for web application security testing.
useWhen: You test an application you are authorized to test and want a reference for one vulnerability class.
skipWhen: You are new to web security or lack authorization. Start with OWASP learning material instead.

oneLiner: A template-based vulnerability scanner that checks targets against community-written YAML templates.
useWhen: You scan systems you are authorized to test and want repeatable, template-driven checks.
skipWhen: You need manual, in-depth testing of business logic. Template scanners find known patterns, not custom flaws.

oneLiner: A fast web fuzzer written in Go for discovering hidden paths, parameters and virtual hosts. Fuzzing means sending many guessed inputs and watching how the server responds.
useWhen: You do authorized content discovery and want speed with flexible response filtering.
skipWhen: You are not authorized to test the target. Aggressive fuzzing can overload servers and trigger alarms.

oneLiner: An interactive HTTPS proxy for inspecting, modifying and replaying traffic between an app and the network.
useWhen: You debug what your own app sends and receives, or test how an API behaves.
skipWhen: You only need simple request tests. A plain HTTP client is quicker. Only intercept traffic from devices and apps you own.

oneLiner: Short, practical guides on secure coding and defense for topics like authentication and input validation.
useWhen: You are writing code and want concise best practices for one security topic.
skipWhen: You need a full threat model or a compliance checklist. These sheets are focused tips, not a complete program.

oneLiner: A tool for running large language models locally, with a simple command line and an API.
useWhen: You want to try or build with open models on your own machine without sending data to a cloud service.
skipWhen: Your hardware is limited. Larger models need a lot of memory, and the largest need a strong GPU.

oneLiner: An open-source backend platform built on Postgres, with auth, storage and APIs.
useWhen: You want a Postgres-based backend with auth and storage quickly and are comfortable with SQL.
skipWhen: You need heavily custom backend logic or no platform dependency. Self-hosting takes real effort.

oneLiner: Accessible React components styled with Tailwind that you copy into your own project.
useWhen: You use React and Tailwind and want full control over the component code.
skipWhen: You want a versioned package you can update with one command. Copied components are yours to maintain.

oneLiner: A workflow automation tool with a visual editor that connects apps and APIs and can be self-hosted.
useWhen: You want to automate repeated tasks between apps and prefer a visual builder you can host yourself.
skipWhen: You need a standard open-source license. Check n8n's license terms before building a commercial product on it.

oneLiner: A framework for building applications with language models: prompts, tools, retrieval and agents.
useWhen: You are building a multi-step LLM application and want ready-made integrations.
skipWhen: Your app is a single model call. Your model provider's SDK is simpler and easier to debug.

oneLiner: An open-source library for interactive vector maps in the browser.
useWhen: You need web maps without Mapbox's license and billing and can supply your own map tiles.
skipWhen: You want a ready-made map with tiles included. You must choose a tile source and style yourself.

oneLiner: A single-file backend with a database, auth, file storage and an admin interface.
useWhen: You want a small backend for a side project or small app, deployed as one binary.
skipWhen: You expect heavy write traffic or need horizontal scaling. It is built around SQLite on one server.

oneLiner: A curated list of free software you can host yourself, grouped by category.
useWhen: You want to replace a paid SaaS tool with something you run yourself.
skipWhen: You don't want to maintain servers, updates and backups. Self-hosting makes those tasks yours.

oneLiner: A curated list of awesome lists, organised by topic.
useWhen: You want to find the best list for a topic before searching on your own.
skipWhen: You need a single answer. Lists point to many options, and quality varies from list to list.
